niche_preference_profile: Prefers interfaces that feel clearly usable, well-structured, and intentionally grouped: strong visible primary actions, distinct card-based sections, clear top-to-bottom hierarchy, readable high-contrast content, and layouts that avoid clutter. They often like polished, premium styling with rounded containers and cohesive surfaces, but only when it does not reduce clarity. They also favor screens that look complete and actionable rather than empty, disabled, or ambiguous.

top_7_criteria.description: Prefers strong top-to-bottom hierarchy with clear emphasis, organized scanning order, separated content blocks, and obvious focal points rather than flat or competing layouts.
Prefers content grouped into distinct cards, rounded containers, or clearly separated sections instead of open, undivided, or weakly bounded layouts.
Prefers large, high-contrast, obviously active primary actions—especially anchored bottom CTAs—over muted, text-only, disabled-looking, or weakly emphasized actions.
Prefers fewer competing UI elements, less decorative noise, and simpler control sets rather than crowded screens with extra chips, badges, dividers, overlays, or redundant controls.
Prefers high-contrast text, clearer labels, stronger separation of information, and easier-to-scan content presentation over low-contrast or visually muddier treatments.
Prefers screens that look finished, populated, and ready to use, with an obvious path to completing the task, rather than empty, ambiguous, blocked, or wireframe-like states.
Prefers refined, cohesive, modern UI surfaces such as soft cards, rounded containers, balanced spacing, and integrated components over rougher, improvised, or utilitarian presentation.
